## Why This Is Asked
This evaluates practical troubleshooting skills for private registry authentication in Kubernetes, a common real-world scenario.

- ImagePullBackOff troubleshooting
- Docker registry secrets management
- Service account configuration
- Image pull strategies

## Code Example
```bash
# Create registry secret
kubectl create secret docker-registry regsecret \
  --docker-server=REGISTRY_URL \
  --docker-username=USERNAME \
  --docker-password=PASSWORD \
  --docker-email=EMAIL

# Apply to default service account

  -p '{"imagePullSecrets": [{"name": "regsecret"}]}'

  -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"imagePullSecrets":[{"name":"regsecret"}]}}}}'
```

- Sidecar pattern for in‑place reload

## Why This Is Asked
Overly broad RBAC can leak secrets across namespaces; this checks detection and remediation under realistic constraints.

## Key Concepts
- RBAC scope (cluster vs namespace)
- kubectl can-i to validate permissions
- Safe remediation: move from ClusterRoleBinding to namespace-scoped RoleBinding

## Code Example
```yaml
# payments namespace only
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: secret-reader
  namespace: payments
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["secrets"]
  verbs: ["get","list"]
```
```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: payments-secret-reader
  namespace: payments
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: <SA_NAME>
  namespace: payments
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: secret-reader
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```
